text:
sophie_support: FYI ticket #C-8422 — customer says their app ran out of monthly credits mid-streaming job, but they expect reset to have happened already. They pasted tenant id and a short timeline. Link: https://support.redwood.ai/ticket/C-8422

meera_billing: pulling the ledger and invoice snapshots now. quick check: tenant shows a reset window at 2024-08-01T00:00:00+00:00 (org-level). customer timezone is America/Los_Angeles. Could be a TZ confusion.

jon_prodeng: can you paste the raw headers or client logs? want to see if client did reconnect/retry loops — retries can double-count tokens in some older SDK versions.

sophie_support: pasted excerpt from customer logs (they scrubbed token):

```
2024-07-31T23:58:12Z websocket open
2024-08-01T00:00:05-07:00 reconnect attempt (code 1006)
2024-08-01T00:00:06-07:00 sdk retry send chunk id=42
2024-08-01T00:00:07-07:00 received 200 OK (duplicate)
```

sophie_support: they say UI showed 0 credits at 00:00 local, but billing says reset at 07:00 UTC. customer assumed reset is midnight local.

jon_prodeng: that log snippet is super useful. two things to check: (1) whether the streaming session counted prefix tokens on reconnect, (2) whether our quota-display cache invalidated earlier than the actual reset. i'll grep quota-service logs for tenant id.

quota-bot: automated alert: quota-cache-invalidate tenant=ten-72ef occurred at 2024-08-01T00:00:00-07:00 (cache TTL expiry).

devops_maya: note — for hosted tenants we display a cached "visible_credits" value in the console that is TTLed at 5 minutes to reduce DB load. If the cache was invalidated right before the reset window in UTC it could show zero briefly while the backend was still reconciling.

meera_billing: ledger shows last refill event at 2024-08-01T07:00:09Z. No refund events. So tokens were actually refilled at 07:00Z, which is 00:00 PDT — wait math: 07:00Z == 00:00 PDT. that matches customer's expectation actually. hm.

jon_prodeng: ah — the tenant had a rolling-midnight window because of a legacy migration (tenant metadata flagged to use "billing-window-offset=+7h"). i found this in the tenant config: `billing_window_utc_offset_seconds=25200`. That explains 07:00Z behavior. but still doesn't explain exhaustion mid-job.

jon_prodeng: dug into serving logs for the websocket session. found duplicate token accounting on reconnect for streaming chunks in runtime v1.4.2. repro snippet i ran locally: 

```
# reproduce: open websocket, send chunk, force reconnect, observe accounting lines
python reproduce_stream.py --tenant ten-72ef --force-reconnect
# logs:
ACCOUNTING: tenant=ten-72ef delta_tokens=412
ACCOUNTING: tenant=ten-72ef delta_tokens=412  # duplicate on reconnect
```

jon_prodeng: looks like a double-count bug when reconnection occurs within the same logical stream. created PR to add idempotency key on chunk accounting.

meera_billing: recommended next steps for support reply: (1) explain reset timing — confirm tenant actually has refill at 07:00Z and show ledger snapshot, (2) explain UI cache TTL and why console may have shown zero, (3) acknowledge double-count bug and offer to run a one-time compensation while fix rolls out, (4) ask for customer SDK version and recommend upgrade to our patched client when released.

sophie_support: agreed. i'll draft the reply and offer a temporary credits grant to make them whole. also asking customer to share exact SDK version so we can correlate. :handshake: 

devops_maya: ops note — schedule a quick patch to make accounting idempotent and add extra telemetry for reconnect flows. created runbook ticket OPS-1145.

sophie_support: closing the internal thread, will follow up in public ticket with the customer and loop in billing once they confirm acceptance of compensation.
